code_quality.notes: The diff is 4 lines in one test file and is byte-for-byte identical to the design's fences (shipped lines 57 and 77 == the M1 fence, lines 61 and 80 == the M2 fence; verified by extraction, not by eye). The new check is correctly placed after 'ident.set_held(true); ident.update_candidates()' (the call that refreshes the occlusion BVH) and after 'demo.look_direction("forward")' (camera.follow is a snap, so the camera really is at the eye). It reuses the product's own BVH and the camera's forward, so it cannot disagree with the I candidates about the ship geometry. Three deductions: (1) the check tests the camera's CENTRE ray, which equals the candidate's ray only because the arrival puts the destination exactly at the screen centre - I measured body pixel (32.0, 32.0) of a 64x64 viewport and body_ray == centre ray (dot 1.000000000); the design's claim that the check 'cannot disagree with them about what blocks' is therefore true only in this scenario. (2) The guard covers only the ship-BVH half of the I contract: the candidates are also filtered by the sky renderer's sv.occludes_direction (ui/ship_star_identification.gd:96 and :127), which the check never consults, so a sky-occlusion failure still surfaces only as the opaque I-check FAIL. (3) The guard's correctness depends on two undocumented orderings in the test file itself (must follow update_candidates()'s BVH refresh and look_direction()'s camera move) - my order mutant shows the check silently degrades to 'ok' when it is moved earlier.

non_blocking: AC1 could not be reproduced green in this clone: 'make free-nav-stop-test' ends 'free-nav-stop: 38 passed, 16 failures', all 16 in the later legs and all downstream of the sim bridge's 2000 ms 'step_timeout' deadline. The base test file in the same clone gives '27 passed, 23 failures' - worse, and the same failure mode - so the redness is pre-existing/environmental, not caused by the diff. Likely environmental cause: this clone has no data/sky textures (164 MB, D-18 'make sky-assets'). Before landing, the controller should re-run AC1 on a host with the sky assets present; the sprint's own six checks are green in my run (AC2 rc 0).

The new guard covers only the ship-BVH half of the I contract. The I candidates are also filtered by the sky renderer's sv.occludes_direction (ui/ship_star_identification.gd:96 and :127); the clear-eye check never consults it, so a sky-occlusion failure would still surface only as the opaque 'I offers ...' FAIL. The design's sentence 'it uses the same BVH and the same eye as the I candidates, so it cannot disagree with them about what blocks' is too strong.

The guard's correctness depends on two orderings that the test file does not document (only the sprint plan does): it must follow 'ident.set_held(true); ident.update_candidates()' (which refreshes the occlusion BVH) and 'demo.look_direction("forward")' (which moves the camera to the eye). My order mutant shows the check silently turning into 'ok' while the eye is blocked. A one-line comment at each check would protect the guard.

The design's own open risk - the x=11 ray's clearance is unmeasured - is now measured: the course face sits at x=8.582 and the centre ray stays clear only up to a +0.5 m shift of the monitor (blocked from +0.6 m), i.e. roughly 0.5-0.6 m of lateral clearance. The guard would catch a future move (good), but the deck-layout row should get the number, and the design's 'not measured as a margin' risk should be closed with it.

The player-visible half of the problem is deferred, not fixed: from the natural arrival eye (the lift's landing, (8, 82, -4.8)) the course screen still hides the destination and holding I still offers nothing. The row discloses this in 'Open questions for the user' and routes it to the deck-layout row / D-148's family, so nothing is hidden - but the row's framing 'the product is behaving correctly' holds only under the I-contract, and no part of this diff makes the arrival view usable.

Documentation inconsistencies: the design's Status line still says 'Revision 1' although the body documents 'Revision 2 (controller, narrow-refinement carve-out; no round 3)'; the sprint JSON's MS2 evidence cites 'Scratch logs in /tmp (7ak_r1.log, 7ak_r2.log, 7ak_r3.log)' although the plan (D1) says /tmp was blocked and the scratch was re-rooted into the tree - neither location holds those logs now; the plan's m1 cmp proof reads 'awk NR==57||NR==76' where the shipped second eye line is 77; the changelog fragment names row 7ak but not the sprint id R1-7AK-FREE-NAV-STOP-EYE that the plan's MS3 command asked for.

The 'not the hidden catalogue point' half of the I check still has no killing mutant (the design's own F2): my R3 mutation only exercises the body-gathering half. The second clause of the check remains unverified; a future change could let the catalogue point back into the candidates and the check would not catch it.

The I check still offers the destination as its finite body from an eye the shipped deck keeps clear, and the base red (40 candidates / 'alpha Cen A is inspectable at its stop') reproduces exactly, so the fix removes a real failure instead of moving the test around it. The whole target could not be shown green in this clone, but the base is worse in the same session with the same step_timeout cascade, so the redness is environmental. Score 81/100, PASS.
